name: Lost Rigger Cove
summary: At Lost Rigger Cove, pirate ships take shape along Tanaris's eastern cliffs. Desert mountains shield the hidden port on three sides, where the Southsea Pirates keep docks and fortified camps beside their shipyard.

sections.title: Pirates and Mountain Walls
sections.body: Rock walls guard almost every side of Lost Rigger Cove. Here on Kalimdor's southeastern edge, the Southsea Freebooters haul salvage and build fresh hulls under Gadgetzan's nose. Cutthroats, dockworkers, and brigands work from this stronghold. From here, Southsea power reaches across the Great Sea, and its pirates raid trade routes between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and coastal settlements.

sections.title: Rivals on the Doorstep
sections.body: Gadgetzan and nearby Steamwheedle Port oppose the Southsea Pirates at their doorstep. The goblins resent the raiders, so they pay mercenaries to slaughter them, thin their ranks, and disrupt their operations.

aliases: who lives in lost rigger cove
faq.answer: The Southsea Pirates hold Lost Rigger Cove. This infamous maritime syndicate ranges across Kalimdor and the South Seas. It uses the natural harbor to repair its fleet and build new warships.

faq.q: Who is fighting the pirates here?
faq.answer: The goblins of Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port fight the pirates. Resenting raiders on their doorstep, they hire passing adventurers to strike at the stronghold and thin the Southsea ranks.

faq.q: Where is Lost Rigger Cove located?
aliases: how to get to lost rigger cove
faq.answer: Lost Rigger Cove lies along Tanaris's eastern coast, southeast of Gadgetzan. A winding canyon path crosses the coastal mountain barrier and leads there.

faq.q: What are the pirates building in the cove?
faq.answer: The Southsea Pirates are building a large ocean-going war vessel. Carpenters and brigands assemble its hull in an active drydock and shipyard at the cove's center.

angles.text: As a rogue, you find a sprawling pirate camp with pockets to pick, private lockboxes, and cutthroats skilled in every dirty trick of maritime swashbuckling.
As a gnome, you can read the pirates' drydock as a crude display of salvaged machinery and stolen parts. It threatens every merchant vessel on the southern seas.
